headline: 481 killed in August road crashes: Road crash deaths rose in August
summary: A total of 513 road crashes were recorded, leaving 664 people injured. Motorcyclists accounted for the largest share of the fatalities.
details: Road crash deaths rose across the country in August, with 481 people killed and 664 injured in 513 crashes, according to the Road Safety Foundation (RSF). This is approximately 65 more deaths than in July.

Motorcyclists were the most affected, with 176 people killed in 183 crashes, accounting for 36.59% of all road deaths. Pedestrians accounted for 102 deaths, while 67 drivers and their assistants died.
The victims included 61 students, 61 women, 58 children, 27 political party leaders, and various professionals including teachers, doctors, and journalists.
Dhaka division recorded the highest number of crashes (172) and deaths (144), while Bogura district saw the highest death toll with 37 fatalities.
Loss of vehicle control (38%) and head-on collisions were the primary causes of crashes. Other factors included pedestrians being hit or run over and rear-end collisions.

The RSF identified excessive speed, reckless driving, faulty vehicles, and poor road design as major causes. They recommended technology-based speed monitoring, better driver training, and reforms to road safety institutions.

headline_marked: 8 more [[arrested for murder of Savar SI]]
headline: 8 more arrested for murder of Savar SI
summary: RAB has detained 8 additional suspects in connection with the killing of a police officer in Savar, bringing the total number of arrests to 9.
details: Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) announced on Monday that 8 more suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of a Sub-Inspector (SI) in Savar.
The arrests were carried out by RAB-10 and RAB-4, with four suspects apprehended from Sadarghat and another four from other locations.
During initial questioning, it was revealed that one suspect, Alauddin, physically assaulted the victim, while another named Jihady had allegedly stabbed the victim with a knife.
RAB officials stated that suspects Apun and Jihady were leaders of a 'teen gang' and were also involved in drug-related activities.
One other suspect, Imran, was reportedly involved in the mob lynching part of the attack.
All 9 arrested individuals are named suspects in the case's First Information Report (FIR).
RAB officials confirmed that they are continuing efforts to arrest the remaining 6 suspects involved in the case.
caption:
8 more suspects arrested in the killing of a Savar SI. Total arrests now stand at 9.

Rapid Action Battalion (RAB) announced on Monday that 8 more suspects have been arrested in connection with the murder of a Sub-Inspector (SI) in Savar.

The arrests were carried out by RAB-10 and RAB-4, with four suspects apprehended from Sadarghat and another four from other locations.

During initial questioning, it was revealed that one suspect, Alauddin, physically assaulted the victim, while another named Jihady had allegedly stabbed the victim with a knife.

RAB officials stated that suspects Apun and Jihady were leaders of a 'teen gang' and were also involved in drug-related activities.

One other suspect, Imran, was reportedly involved in the mob lynching part of the attack.

All 9 arrested individuals are named suspects in the case's First Information Report (FIR).

RAB officials confirmed that they are continuing efforts to arrest the remaining 6 suspects involved in the case.

Source: Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV, Prothom Alo
